column1: # How each monitor capture becomes gate rows (`prove`, docs/MONITOR.md): metadata only (source ids, capture keys,
# gate files, entries, members, points), never a printed time. One line a row to add per capture whose days the gate
# does not hold yet at that row's entry, member and point; every row is split=test (held out).
# What a row reads is never written here: its columns, zone, format, school and clock come from its family, the latest
# row of the same gate file, entry, member and point that reads an earlier capture of the same source and key; else
# such a row whose table prints the same as the capture on every day both hold; else the fetcher's own metadata in the
# monitor's index. A convention changed in a gate file is therefore inherited by the next capture.
# - capture: the index keys (`*` any run of characters).
# - entry: `index` (the capture's own entry as the index names it, read at its unit's point when it names one, else at
#   its own), `same` (every row of the gate file that reads an earlier capture of this source and key, cloned: its
#   entry, member and point; with member * and point same), or an entry (`id` or `id/unit`).
# - member: `-`, `index` (the index's entry is the member: a cautious entry's member row), or a member id.
# - point: `index`, `unit` (the unit's own point), `all` (every point the gate file reads this entry and member at),
# - days: `all`; `month` (the month the capture's key ends with, yyyy-mm: a cautious entry's members for the month a
#   member published); `excused` (without the days the gate file's @excuse lines excuse for the member, ruling R117).
# - from: `-` (the capture itself) or another capture, `<source>/<key>` with {yyyy} and {mm} from this capture's key.
# A line whose capture is the bare `*` does not apply to a capture another line of the same source and gate file names
# more specifically: Kemenag's fetcher names the five kota of the round of 29 September 2026 by their point alone, and
# the gate holds them as units, so each is given its unit on a line of its own.
# A source's own entry is read at a named point, never `all`: Amman's region table at Amman's point alone (ruling R30,
# a table checked for the place it is printed for), however many other points jo.awqaf is read at; `all` is for the
# cautious members, whose table is the member's for every point of the entry.
# Not here: the hand-read sources (manual in sources.tsv), the Mawaqit surveys (calendars, checked by their surveys),
# and members no fetcher reads (Cape Town's community calendar, masjids.co.za's relay: read by hand each month).
# London Unified: one table for the whole M25 (ruling R44), so a new year is read at every point the gate file reads LUPT at, the unit's own and the twelve edges, as the 2026 rows are.
# Ruling R297: London Unified's table read across the whole M25 (gb-london-lupt-reach.tsv, ReachAreas.AREAS), a new year at every point of the claim too.
# A district new to the fetcher has no earlier monitor capture to clone: the 62 il centres of the round of 12–13 November
# 2026 (ruling R202) stand on tables read by hand (archive/tables/held/tr-diyanet/). The index names each one's unit, so
# this line reads its capture at the unit's own point; its family is the hand-read row, whose table prints the same on
# every day both hold. A key the line above already clones at its unit is planned once (the same row).
# FIDS prints Diyanet Zürich's table (Europe.kt, the review of track T4): each new Zürich capture is FIDS's too.
# The printed imsak (ruling R284, the second audit's G25): JAKIM's and Kemenag's fetchers keep each table's imsak as its own
# capture, `<key>-imsak` (two columns, the Subuh and the imsak, the layout of the hand read-backs under
# archive/tables/imsak/), and only a line whose pattern ends `-imsak` reads it (Recipe.matches). Each new year is held
# where the gate files already hold the imsak: every JAKIM zone at its unit, and the eighteen Kemenag kab/kota of
# id-kemenag-imsak.tsv at theirs (the other units' imsak is checked by the monitor's own check, not yet held).
# Ruling R297: MUIS's table read across the whole of Singapore (sg-muis-reach.tsv, ReachAreas.AREAS), each capture at every point of the claim too.
# ESA's 30 towns Dar al-Ifta republishes a month at a time, each named: a town's whole month becomes its own row. Not the
# bare `*`: the 48 cities ESA's daily page alone prints (egypt.py's ESA_CITIES, kept since 13 Nov 2026, audit finding F25)
# have no line here, on purpose. Their growing tables hold the one day each run reads, six days in seven never compared:
# the monitor's own check reads every such day at the town's point (an early start is raised on every run), but a day
# sampled is no gate row, so a stamp never says a town was checked through a day between days nothing compared (About's
# "checked through"), and the Ramadan guard never counts the sample as its month being watched (ruling R185 (b)). Their
# 2027 days come from ESA's pages read by hand (sources.tsv, eg-esa-2027).
# The reach rows (sa-ummalqura-reach.tsv, kz-qmdb-reach.tsv; generateReachRows): each measured unit's own table
# replayed across its reach, a line per unit, so that each new year of a unit's table is read at every point of
# its reach too (`all`: the points the reach file reads that unit at). The pattern ends `-2*` so that a place's
# key never names another's (riyadh-2027, not riyadh-al-khabra-2027).
# Ruling R300: Tayma's table read within a minute's reach of the town as well (sa-ummalqura-tayma-reach.tsv, ReachAreas.AREAS), a new year at every point of the claim too.
# The Kyrgyz Muftiate's localities (kg-default-reach.tsv, the Kyrgyz round's review of 12 Nov 2026): each locality's own
# table replayed across its reach, and Aravan town's (the Aravan table, read across the town's reach).
# Kemenag's kab/kota (id-kemenag-reach.tsv, the review of 12 Nov 2026): each unit's new year read across its circle
# as its own point's rows are, a line per unit by the fetcher's key.
# Kemenag's second round of 12 Nov 2026 (KemenagKabkota.kt's round2): each unit's new year read across its circle, as the round's.
# IRN is read by hand each December since ruling R189 (sources.tsv: manual), so no capture arrives for these three recipes; they rest here for the day bonnetid.info serves plain tables again.
# IRN's Oslo and Trondheim calendars are also no.cautious's member rows (no-cautious.tsv, member no.irn, at IRN's own points); Tromsø is not a no.cautious member row.

# Prove adds a capture only where it holds days the gate does not: the 2026 captures add nothing beside the hand-read off-irn-*-2026.txt rows (a prove dry run of 12 Nov 2026), a new year's capture its row.
# no.cautious has no fixed point, so each is read at IRN's own point as its hand-read row is (a prove dry run of 12 Nov 2026 found `index` read as `unit`, which the gate refuses).
# ESA's towns (eg-esa-reach.tsv, ruling R181 of 13 Nov 2026): each monitored town's growing table read across its reach
# as its own point's rows are, a line per town by the fetcher's key (the town's unit id).
# JAKIM's zone towns (my-jakim-cities.tsv, rulings R225-R226): e-solat prints one table for a whole zone, so each
# new year of a zone's table is read at the own point of every city of the app's list on that zone's list too
# (`all`: the points the towns file reads that zone at), a line per zone that has such towns. The bare line above
# still reads every capture at its zone's unit in my-jakim.tsv: these name another gate file, so it applies as before.
# And the zone towns' imsak rows (my-jakim-cities.tsv reads each town's imsak beside its day's table): a line per zone.
# Türkiye's 84 il centres (tr-diyanet-reach.tsv, ruling R255 of 14 Nov 2026): every unit's growing table is read across
# its reach as its own point's rows are, under the same pinned copy as the own row, so the reach still replays every own
# table. Two lines, as for tr-diyanet.tsv above. The first clones the reach rows that already read an earlier capture
# of the same key, at each point they stand at; it needs nothing from the monitor's index, which still names nine of
# the older keys (antalya, bursa, catalca, diyarbakir, gaziantep, izmir, konya, sile, silivri) as bare `tr.diyanet` at
# a point until the fetcher's next run rewrites it (the fetcher names all 84 by unit since ruling R202). The second
# reads a capture at `all` the points the reach file reads its unit at, the unit taken from the index: the only way in
# for the 62 il centres of 12–13 November 2026, whose reach rows stand on tables read by hand and so have no earlier
# capture to clone; a capture whose index line names no unit is not read by it (the first line reads it). A row both
# lines call for is planned once. A row is added only for a capture that holds days the point does not hold yet.
# A new day later than a unit's limit at a point of its reach is left out and the unit demoted (ruling R185) until its
# limits are measured again (docs/MONITOR.md, "Türkiye's limits"): the 62 il centres of 12–13 November 2026 were
# The second trust audit's G26 (14 Nov 2026, ruling R270): the reach rows of every other entry whose measured units reach
# past their own points. A new capture of a table a unit is checked on at its own point is read at every point of that
# unit's reach too: a year-named table by the unit at `all` the reach's points, a table the fetcher grows under one key
# (Habous's months, Amman's, Cape Town's MJC month, Diyanet's Zürich read as FIDS's) by cloning the reach rows that read
# Diyanet's European cities joined the gate on 16 Nov 2026 (ruling R293): a new Diyanet city capture is read at every
# point of its reach by cloning the reach rows that read its earlier capture.
# Every other zone's reach (ruling R287): the other 50 zones, most of them read by hand from e-solat on 13 Nov 2026
# (archive/tables/manual/my-jakim/, archive/tables/imsak/my-jakim/2026-11-13/), have no earlier capture to clone and
# no line of their own above. A capture of such a zone (its day's table, then its printed imsak, `-imsak`, which only
# a pattern so named reads) is read at `all` the reach file's points of the unit the index names, as Türkiye's second
# reach line is; the bare `*` stands aside for the ten zones named above (Labuan's WLY02 the tenth, since the
# monitor's capture of its 2027 table on 23 Nov 2026), and a row both imsak lines call for is planned once. Without
# them a zone's next year would grow its own rows alone and CityUnitsTest would halt prove.
# Ruling R310: each JAKIM zone read across all the ground the app hands it (my-jakim-zones-reach.tsv, ReachAreas.AREAS):
# a new year of a zone is read at every point of the zone's claim too, by the same lines as its reach rows above.
# The zones a place of the app takes with no town of the zone's list (my-jakim-cities.tsv since G28, ruling R274): its rows grow with each capture as the towns' do.
